concepts.title: Structure and Classification of Amines
concepts.definition: Amines arise when one, two or all three hydrogens of ammonia are swapped for alkyl or aryl groups; the trivalent nitrogen stays sp3 hybridised with a lone pair in the fourth orbital, giving a pyramidal shape with the C-N-E angle squeezed just under 109.5 degrees, and the products divide into primary, secondary and tertiary classes.
concepts.key_idea: Amines are called simple when all groups match and mixed when they differ; quaternary ammonium salts form when nitrogen takes a fourth group and a positive charge.
question_patterns: classify (CH3)2CHNH2, CH3NHCH(CH3)2 and (CH3CH2)2NCH3 as primary, secondary or tertiary amines

solution_steps.explain: one alkyl or aryl group gives a primary amine, two a secondary, three a tertiary
sp3 nitrogen with one lone pair forces the pyramidal molecular shape

concepts.title: Naming Amines in Both Systems
concepts.definition: Common names glue the alkyl word to amine (methylamine) with di- and tri- prefixes for repeats, while IUPAC renames primary amines as alkanamines and pins nitrogen substituents with N- locants; aniline doubles as benzenamine, and multi-NH2 chains carry diamine or triamine endings.
concepts.key_idea: CH3NHCH2CH3 reads N-methylethanamine because the longer chain becomes the parent and the methyl rides on nitrogen.
question_patterns: write the IUPAC name of CH3NHCH(CH3)2
give the systematic name for trimethylamine

solution_steps.action: promote the longest chain to parent
solution_steps.explain: the parent takes the -amine ending; extra hydrocarbon groups on nitrogen get N- locants
keep the hydrocarbon -e and add -diamine with carbon locants for two or more NH2 groups

concepts.title: Preparing Amines: Nitro Reduction and Ammonolysis
concepts.definition: Nitro compounds drop to amines under H2 with Ni, Pd or Pt or with metal-acid couples where iron and HCl are favoured; alkyl or benzyl halides undergo ammonolysis with ethanolic ammonia in a sealed tube at 373 K, giving a primary amine that keeps alkylating unless ammonia is in large excess.
concepts.key_idea: Ammonolysis always mixes classes (primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary salt), so flooding with ammonia pins the product at the primary amine.
question_patterns: why is iron scrap with hydrochloric acid preferred for reducing nitrobenzene to aniline
write the reaction of ethanolic ammonia with ethyl chloride

solution_steps.action: match the precursor to the reducing system
solution_steps.explain: nitro groups, nitriles and amides all accept hydrogen or hydride to reach RNH2
each amine product is itself nucleophilic, so ratio control decides the class isolated

concepts.title: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis Limits
concepts.definition: Phthalimide's potassium salt, made with ethanolic KOH, attacks a primary alkyl halide and alkaline hydrolysis then releases a clean primary amine; aryl halides refuse the substitution, so aniline-type amines cannot come from this route.
concepts.key_idea: The method's value is purity: no secondary or tertiary amine ever forms because the nitrogen is locked inside the imide until hydrolysis.
question_patterns: why does Gabriel phthalimide synthesis fail for aromatic primary amines

solution_steps.explain: ethanolic KOH deprotonates phthalimide, creating the nucleophilic potassium salt
the anion attacks only primary alkyl halides (never aryl), and alkaline hydrolysis cuts the amine free

concepts.title: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation Carbon Count
concepts.definition: Bromine in aqueous or ethanolic NaOH migrates the amide's alkyl or aryl group from the carbonyl carbon onto nitrogen, releasing a primary amine that carries one carbon fewer than the amide it came from.
concepts.key_idea: Counting backwards fixes the starting amide: a three-carbon amine demands a four-carbon amide such as butanamide.
question_patterns: propanamine has 3 carbons; how many carbons must the amide contain for its Hoffmann degradation to give it

solution_steps.explain: the group migrates off the carbonyl, so only the R portion reaches nitrogen

concepts.title: Boiling Points and Solubility Trends of Amines
concepts.definition: Hydrogen bonding lifts boiling points in the order primary > secondary > tertiary for isomeric amines because tertiary molecules carry no N-H to donate, and everything trails the corresponding alcohol whose O-H bonds are stronger; water solubility fades as the hydrophobic alkyl bulk grows.
concepts.key_idea: Butan-1-ol out-dissolves butan-1-amine because oxygen's higher electronegativity makes stronger hydrogen bonds to water.
question_patterns: arrange C2H5OH, (CH3)2NH and C2H5NH2 by rising boiling point

solution_steps.explain: primary amines offer two hydrogen-bond donors, secondary one, tertiary none
each extra carbon drowns the polar head, cutting water solubility step by step

concepts.title: Basic Strength Orders of Amines
concepts.definition: Alkyl groups push electron density onto nitrogen so aliphatic amines out-base ammonia, but in water solvation and steric crowding scramble the simple inductive order: methyl amines run secondary > primary > tertiary while ethyl analogues run secondary > tertiary > primary, and aniline trails badly because its lone pair resonates into the ring leaving the anilinium ion with fewer resonance structures.
concepts.key_idea: Electron-releasing ring substituents such as OCH3 raise arylamine basicity while NO2, SO3H, COOH and halogens lower it.
question_patterns: arrange C6H5NH2, C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH and NH3 in falling order of basic strength

solution_steps.action: test where the lone pair sits
solution_steps.explain: alkyl push raises availability; ring resonance drains it, so arylamines weaken
bigger ammonium ions hydrogen-bond less with water, so aqueous orders mix steric and solvation effects with the +I trend

concepts.title: Base Strength Ratio from pKb Values
concepts.definition: Each pKb hides a base-ten gap: raising ten to minus pKb recovers Kb, so dividing one constant by the other counts how many times a stronger amine out-bases a weaker one in water.
concepts.key_idea: Bigger pKb always means the weaker base; Table 9.3 spans about 3.0 for dialkylamines to 9.4 for aniline.

concepts.title: Alkylation, Acylation and Benzoylation of Amines
concepts.definition: Amines swing at alkyl halides as nucleophiles, climbing the class ladder toward quaternary salts, and swap an N-H hydrogen for an acyl group when acid chlorides, anhydrides or esters attack, building amides in pyridine so the HCl by-product is soaked up; benzoyl chloride performs the same trick as benzoylation.
concepts.key_idea: Amines merely salt carboxylic acids at room temperature; the acyl chloride or anhydride is needed to push all the way to the amide.
question_patterns: what is the final alkylation product when aniline reacts with excess methyl iodide in sodium carbonate solution

solution_steps.explain: the lone pair displaces halide or carboxylate from the alkyl or acyl substrate
a stronger base such as pyridine traps HCl and pulls the equilibrium to products

concepts.title: Tests That Separate Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Amines
concepts.definition: Chloroform with alcoholic KOH hands primary amines alone a foul isocyanide (carbylamine test); benzenesulphonyl chloride gives an alkali-soluble sulphonamide with primary amines, an alkali-insoluble one with secondary amines and nothing at all with tertiary amines (Hinsberg's method); and nitrous acid releases nitrogen quantitatively from primary aliphatic amines while aromatic ones keep their stable diazonium salts at 273-278 K.
concepts.key_idea: Nitrous acid made in situ from NaNO2 and mineral acid is the reagent that sorts all three classes plus aromatic from aliphatic in one sweep.
question_patterns: which amines answer the carbylamine test and what is smelled

solution_steps.explain: only NH2 nitrogens build the isocyanide, so a stink convicts a primary amine
the acidic N-H of the primary product dissolves in NaOH while the secondary product and the untouched tertiary stay out of solution

concepts.title: Electrophilic Substitution on the Aniline Ring
concepts.definition: The NH2 group floods the ortho and para positions with electron density, so bromine water drops 2,4,6-tribromoaniline at once; acetylating the nitrogen tempers this power for clean monosubstitution, direct nitration muddles meta product through anilinium formation, and salt build-up with AlCl3 shuts aniline out of Friedel-Crafts reactions.
concepts.key_idea: Acetylation to acetanilide parks the lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen, weakening activation just enough to steer the incoming electrophile.
question_patterns: what white precipitate appears when aniline meets bromine water

solution_steps.explain: resonance from nitrogen piles electron density at ortho and para, inviting electrophiles there
acetylate, substitute, then hydrolyse the amide back to the amine

concepts.title: Diazotisation and Displacement of the Diazonium Group
concepts.definition: Aniline plus nitrous acid at 273-278 K builds benzenediazonium chloride, whose N2+ group departs as gas while Cl, Br or CN arrive through Sandmeyer's copper(I) route, Gatterman's copper powder variant delivers halogens, KI installs iodine, fluoroborate heating gives fluoride, hypophosphorous acid or ethanol restores plain arene, warming hydrolyses to phenol, and copper with sodium nitrite installs NO2.
concepts.key_idea: The diazonium route reaches fluorides, iodides and cyanides that direct halogenation or SNi chemistry on chlorobenzene cannot touch.
question_patterns: write the diazotisation of aniline with sodium nitrite and HCl below 278 K

concepts.title: Coupling Reactions and Azo Dye Formation
concepts.definition: Kept cold, the diazonium ion acts as a weak electrophile that couples at the para position of phenols or anilines, stringing two rings through an N=N link and producing the coloured azo compounds behind many dyes, such as p-hydroxyazobenzene and p-aminoazobenzene.
concepts.key_idea: The extended conjugation across the azo bond absorbs visible light, which is why coupling products serve as dyes.
question_patterns: write the coupling reaction of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol

solution_steps.explain: retention of the diazo group, not displacement, drives coupling

solution_steps.explain: the phenol or aniline ring donates at its para position to build the N=N bridge
